identity.title: The Detection of Hot Molecular Cores in the Small Magellanic Cloud

paper_type_evidence.quote: We observed two high-mass young stellar objects in the SMC with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array, and detected emission lines of CO, HCO$^+$, H$^{13}$CO$^+$, SiO, H$_2$CO, CH$_3$OH, SO, and SO$_2$.

Observations were made with ALMA in 2019 and 2022 as a Cycle 7 program (2019.1.01770.S, PI: K. Tanaka), which is a part of the “Magellanic Clouds Outflow and Chemistry Survey (MAGOS)” project, in which we observed 10 sources in the SMC and 30 sources in the LMC.
We also use the ALMA archival data, 2019.1.00534.S (PI: S. Zahorecz).

question.value: To detect hot molecular cores in the low-metallicity environment (0.2 solar metallicity) of the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) and investigate the effect of metallicity on the chemical evolution and molecular abundances of protostellar sources.

evidence.quote: We report the first detection of hot molecular cores in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC), a nearby dwarf galaxy with 0.2 solar metallicity.
Obtaining a comprehensive view of chemical compositions of hot cores at various metallicities should help understand the effect of the metallicity on the chemical evolution of protostellar sources.

Observations were made with ALMA in 2019 and 2022 as a Cycle 7 program (2019.1.01770.S, PI: K. Tanaka), which is a part of the “Magellanic Clouds Outflow and Chemistry Survey (MAGOS)” project, in which we observed 10 sources in the SMC and 30 sources in the LMC.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA$\#$2019.1.01770.S and 2019.1.00534.S.
We also use the ALMA archival data, 2019.1.00534.S (PI: S. Zahorecz).

analysis_steps.goal: Measure spatial distributions and deconvolved source sizes

method.value: Construct integrated intensity images over velocity ranges of detected emission (stacking lines with similar E_u for SO2 and CH3OH); fit 2D Gaussian to emission peak and compute deconvolved source size by subtracting beam size in quadrature.

evidence.quote: The images are constructed by integrating spectral data in the velocity range where the emission is detected.
For SO$_2$ and CH$_3$OH, several emission lines with similar upper state energies are stacked to reduce the noise level.

We also estimated the deconvolved source sizes as $\sqrt{\mathrm{FWHM_{maj}} \times \mathrm{FWHM_{min}} - \Theta_{\mathrm{beam}}^2 }$, where $\mathrm{FWHM_{maj/min}}$ is the major/minor FWHM size as estimated from the two-dimensional Gaussian fit, and $\Theta_{\mathrm{beam}}^2$ is the geometric mean of the beam major and minor axes.

findings_qualitative.value: First detection of hot molecular cores in the SMC (S07 and S09), demonstrating that hot-core formation is a common phenomenon during high-mass star formation across 0.2-1 Z_sun.

evidence.quote: We report the first detection of hot molecular cores in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC), a nearby dwarf galaxy with 0.2 solar metallicity.

This work, in conjunction with previous hot-core studies in the LMC and outer/inner Galaxy, suggests that the formation of a hot core would be a common phenomenon during high-mass star formation across the metallicity range of $0.2$–$1{\rm\:}Z_\odot$.

findings_qualitative.value: High-excitation SO2 lines trace compact (~0.1 pc), hot (>100 K) gas in the SMC hot cores and serve as a reliable low-metallicity hot-core tracer, whereas CH3OH is extended (~0.2-0.3 pc) and cool (~39 K).

evidence.quote: Compact hot-core regions are traced by SO$_2$, whose spatial extent is about $0.1{\rm\:pc}$, and the gas temperature is higher than 100 K based on the rotation diagram analysis. In contrast, CH$_3$OH, a classical hot-core tracer, is dominated by extended ($\sim$0.2–0.3${\rm\:pc}$) components in both sources, and the gas temperature is estimated to be 39$^{+8}_{-6}$ K for one source.
High-excitation SO$_2$ lines will be a useful hot-core tracer in the low-metallicity environments of the SMC and LMC.

findings_qualitative.value: Protostellar outflows are detected as high-velocity CO(3-2) components in both S07 and S09, with S09 being the second CO-traced protostellar outflow found in the SMC.

evidence.quote: Protostellar outflows are also detected from both sources as high-velocity components of CO.
The outflows detected in S09 is the second example of CO-traced protostellar outflows found in the SMC.

claims.hypothesis: Hot molecular cores can form around high-mass young stellar objects even at the 0.2 solar metallicity of the SMC.
claims.experiment: ALMA Band 7 (0.1 pc scale) continuum and molecular line observations toward two SMC high-mass YSOs, S07 and S09, analyzed via Gaussian spatial fitting, rotation diagrams, and dust continuum modeling.
claims.result: Detected compact (~0.1 pc, deconvolved <=0.05-0.09 pc), dense (6-9 x 10^5 cm^-3), and hot (T_rot = 171 K and 146 K in SO2) molecular gas cores associated with high-mass protostars and CO(3-2) outflows.
claims.finding: Hot molecular cores exist in the SMC, indicating that hot-core formation is a common phenomenon during high-mass star formation across 0.2-1 Z_sun.

evidence.quote: Compact hot-core regions are traced by SO$_2$, whose spatial extent is about $0.1{\rm\:pc}$, and the gas temperature is higher than 100 K based on the rotation diagram analysis.

This work, in conjunction with previous hot-core studies in the LMC and outer/inner Galaxy, suggests that the formation of a hot core would be a common phenomenon during high-mass star formation across the metallicity range of $0.2$–$1{\rm\:}Z_\odot$.

claims.hypothesis: SO2 and CH3OH trace different physical regions and desorption/formation mechanisms in the SMC hot cores.
claims.experiment: Compare deconvolved source sizes and rotation temperatures of SO2 and CH3OH, and test correlations of SO2 column density with SO and SiO across SMC, LMC, and Galactic hot cores.
claims.result: SO2 is compact (deconvolved <=0.05 and 0.09 pc) and hot (171 K and 146 K), while CH3OH is extended (deconvolved 0.21 and 0.25 pc) and cooler (39 K in S07). SO2 correlates tightly with SO (r = 0.98) but not with shock tracer SiO (r = 0.32).
claims.finding: SO2 arises from thermal ice sublimation and high-temperature gas-phase chemistry in the compact hot core, whereas extended CH3OH has a non-negligible contribution from non-thermal desorption (e.g., shock sputtering or UV photodesorption).

evidence.loc: SO$_2$ as a tracer of low-metallicity hot cores
evidence.quote: The SO$_2$ column densities show a tight correlation with SO (correlation coefficient: 0.98), while they do not correlate with the strong-shock tracer SiO (correlation coefficient: 0.32). This would suggest that the formation of SO$_2$ in the current sample is mainly induced by the sublimation of sulfur-bearing ices, rather than sputtering by strong shocks.

evidence.loc: SO$_2$ as a tracer of low-metallicity hot cores
evidence.quote: A relatively low temperature and extended spatial distribution of CH$_3$OH suggest that the contribution from a non-thermal desorption is not negligible for its production in both sources.

claims.hypothesis: Chemical formation of SO2 in hot cores is regulated by elemental abundances, while CH3OH abundance is sensitive to local initial star-forming conditions.
claims.experiment: Compare metallicity-scaled fractional abundances of SO2, CH3OH, and other species across SMC (0.2 Z_sun), LMC (0.4 Z_sun), and Galactic (1 Z_sun) hot cores.
claims.result: Metallicity-scaled SO2 abundances are relatively constant among SMC, LMC, and Galactic hot cores, whereas CH3OH shows large source-to-source abundance variations even after metallicity scaling.
claims.finding: SO2 formation is regulated by elemental sulfur/oxygen abundances in high-temperature gas-phase reactions, while CH3OH variation is likely driven by diversity in initial dust temperatures and shielding during the ice-forming stage.

evidence.quote: The metallicity-scaled abundances of SO$_2$ in hot cores are comparable among the SMC, Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC), and Galactic sources, suggesting that the chemical reactions leading to SO$_2$ formation would be regulated by elemental abundances.

As seen in the figure, the CH$_3$OH abundance shows large source-to-source variation even after corrected for the metallicity. In contrast, the metallicity-scaled abundance of SO$_2$ is relatively constant among SMC, LMC, and Galactic sources.

why_this_data.value: The SMC has the lowest metallicity (0.2 Z_sun) among Local-Group star-forming galaxies where ALMA can detect and spatially resolve dense gas tracers at 0.1 pc scales; S07 and S09 are embedded high-mass YSOs with ice absorption bands.

evidence.quote: The SMC harbors the lowest metallicity environment (cite: Hun05; Cho18) among the Local-Group star-forming galaxies where we can detect and spatially resolve dense gas tracers.
The absorption bands of silicate dust, H$_2$O ice, and CO$_2$ ice are detected in both sources, suggesting that they are still embedded in a dense core (cite: Oli13).

why_this_method.value: Rotation diagram analysis allows simultaneous estimation of gas temperature and column density where multiple lines spanning a range of upper-state energies are detected (SO2 in both sources, CH3OH in S07); for S09 SO2, a two-component fit is used because two temperature regimes are clearly seen.

evidence.quote: We use the rotation diagram method to estimate column densities and temperatures of SO$_2$ in both sources and CH$_3$OH in S07 (Figure 2), while the number of detected CH$_3$OH lines in S09 is not sufficient for this purpose.

For SO$_2$ in S09, a straight-line fit is separated into low- and high-temperature regimes ($E_{u}$ $<$60 K and $E_{u}$ $>$60 K), because different temperature components are clearly seen in the diagram.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Formation of SO2 via strong-shock sputtering was considered and rejected in favor of thermal sublimation of sulfur-bearing ices, because SO2 column density correlates tightly with SO (r=0.98) but not with the shock tracer SiO (r=0.32).

evidence.loc: SO$_2$ as a tracer of low-metallicity hot cores
evidence.quote: The SO$_2$ column densities show a tight correlation with SO (correlation coefficient: 0.98), while they do not correlate with the strong-shock tracer SiO (correlation coefficient: 0.32). This would suggest that the formation of SO$_2$ in the current sample is mainly induced by the sublimation of sulfur-bearing ices, rather than sputtering by strong shocks.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: UV photodesorption in an outflow cavity wall as the origin of gaseous CH3OH was considered alongside shock sputtering, with the caveat that laboratory experiments show solid CH3OH dissociates upon UV irradiation.

evidence.loc: SO$_2$ as a tracer of low-metallicity hot cores
evidence.quote: Considering the presence of protostellar outflows (Appendix 9), sputtering of ice mantles by shock (cite: Aot15) or photodesorption by UV photons in an outflow cavity wall of the central protostar may be responsible for the desorption mechanism. Note that the latter mechanism is still under debate, since laboratory experiments have reported that solid CH$_3$OH readily dissociates upon photodesorption by the UV irradiation (cite: Ber16; Cru16).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Assuming CH3OH in S09 has the same rotation temperature as the high-temperature SO2 component was tested, yielding a twice higher CH3OH column density.

evidence.quote: If the rotation temperature of CH$_3$OH in S09 is assumed to be the same as that of the high-temperature component of SO$_2$, then we obtain a twice higher CH$_3$OH column density.

limitations_admitted.value: Only upper limits on deconvolved source sizes can be estimated when the emission size is comparable with or smaller than the beam size.

evidence.quote: Note that only upper limits are estimated for the emission whose size is comparable with or smaller than the beam size.

referee_caveats_inferred: Beam dilution may affect the derived column densities and rotation temperatures since the SO2 hot core in S07 is unresolved (<=0.05 pc vs 0.13 pc beam) while spectral extraction is done over a fixed 0.43'' (0.13 pc) aperture without a beam-filling factor correction.
Optically thin LTE is assumed for all SO2 and CH3OH lines without radiative transfer modeling to check optical depth or sub-thermal excitation.
